concept_html:
A data science project starts as a notebook and a CSV. By month three it has helper modules, tests, a model, and three people asking how to run it. The fix is structure from day one.

pyproject.toml is the one configuration file for a modern Python project. It holds:

  • [project]: name, version, requires-python, and runtime dependencies.
  • [dependency-groups] (PEP 735): named groups for development only, such as test or lint. They never ship with the package. Install one with pip install --group test (pip 25.1 and later).
  • [tool.*] tables for tools: [tool.ruff], [tool.mypy], [tool.pytest.ini_options].

One file replaces setup.py, requirements.txt, setup.cfg, .flake8 and pytest.ini.

The src layout puts importable code under src/:

reach_model/
├── pyproject.toml
├── src/reach_model/        # importable package
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── features.py
│   └── train.py
├── tests/                  # pytest, imports reach_model
├── notebooks/              # exploration; imports reach_model, holds no logic
└── data/                   # small samples only; real data stays out of Git

With src/, Python can only import your package after you install it (pip install -e .). Tests then run against the installed package, exactly as a user or a job would. Without it, tests silently import whatever sits in the working directory, and "works on my machine" follows.

Notebooks explore and present. Functions that matter move into src/, where tests and type checks reach them. A notebook that defines the feature pipeline inline cannot be tested or reused by the training job.

Pin requires-python to the versions you test, for example ">=3.11", so pip refuses an interpreter you never tried.

lines: ├── pyproject.toml         # project, dependency groups, ruff, mypy, pytest
│   ├── features.py        # build_features(), used by training and scoring

exercises.prompt: Write `unpinned(pyproject_text)`. Parse the TOML with the standard library and return, sorted, every entry in `[project].dependencies` that has no version constraint at all (no `=`, `<`, `>`, `~` or `!`). Return an empty list when there is no dependencies key.
exercises.prompt_html: Write unpinned(pyproject_text). Parse the TOML with the standard library and return, sorted, every entry in [project].dependencies that has no version constraint at all (no =, <, >, ~ or !). Return an empty list when there is no dependencies key.
exercises.solution:
import tomllib

CONSTRAINT_CHARS = set("=<>~!")


def unpinned(pyproject_text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Runtime dependencies with no version constraint.

    Args:
        pyproject_text: Contents of pyproject.toml.

    Returns:
        Sorted requirement strings without =, <, >, ~ or !.
    """
    project = tomllib.loads(pyproject_text).get("project", {})
    deps = project.get("dependencies", [])
    return sorted(d for d in deps if not CONSTRAINT_CHARS & set(d))

title: One pyproject.toml and a src layout
why_html:
A team trains a churn model from train.ipynb, which defines build_features() in a cell. The scoring job copies the function into score.py. A month later someone fixes a leakage bug in the notebook version only. Training and scoring now compute features differently, and live accuracy drops 9 points while offline metrics look fine.

With build_features() in src/churn/features.py, imported by both the notebook and the job, one fix reaches both, and one test protects it.
